title: Abrindo conta no banco
reading: Mia is an exchange student, and she is at the bank to open an account.
She has never had a bank account before.
The teller shows her a savings account with good interest.
Mia has never had an overdraft, and she doesn't want one.
She needs to give her signature on the form.
She doesn't need to withdraw any money today.
dialogue: Good morning! How can I help you today?
I'd like to open a bank account. I have never had one before.
No problem. Do you want a savings account or a regular account?
A savings account, please. Is the interest good?
It's two percent. And you can't have an overdraft with this account.
Good, because I have never borrowed money from a bank. I don't want a loan.
That's smart. Please fill out a form, and then give me your signature here.
Done. I've never signed so many papers!
Congratulations! Your account is open, and you can withdraw money today. The card is coming by courier, and you must sign for it.
Perfect. I'm glad my account is open.

title: Revisão: Mudança de cidade
grammar: Revisão: will, going to, used to e present perfect
reading: Kate has lived in this city for ten years, but now she is moving.
She is going to rent a small house near the beach.
The movers have loaded the moving van with cardboard boxes.
She used to hate packing, but she has wrapped everything in bubble wrap.
One box says "fragile", and the boy next door helps carry it.
The dolly can't pass through the doorway, so Kate will unpack the boxes first.
dialogue: Kate, have you finished packing yet? The movers are coming at nine.
Almost. I've packed all the books, but I haven't wrapped the glasses yet.
Use the bubble wrap. I used to break a lot of glasses when I moved.
Good idea. I'm going to put the picnic basket in the van, and the hammock too.
Don't forget the trail map. You'll want it near the new house.
Right! The beach has great trails. I'll hike every Sunday, and it will be my new habit.
That sounds great. Have you ever lived near the sea before?
No, never. I'm a little nervous, and the noise of the waves will be new for me.
You'll love it. The streets are quiet, and the speed limit is low.
Yes, it's a calm place, and I think I'm going to be happy there.

title: Um mês de treino para a corrida
reading: Ana has been running every morning for a month.
Her new sneakers are light, and her stopwatch is always in her pocket.
At first, her stride was short and her pace was slow.
Now she stretches her ankle every day, so her sore muscles feel fine.
Yesterday her shoelace came loose, so she stopped and tied it.
Her coach smiled and said, “Nice stride, Ana! Keep it up!”
dialogue: Ben, you look tired. What have you been doing?
I'm training for the city race, and my ankle hurts a little.
Really? How long have you been running?
I've been running every morning for three weeks, and I sweat a lot!
Wow! Do you use a stopwatch to check your pace?
Yes, I do. Yesterday I got a cramp, so I stopped for a minute.
Don't worry. Sore muscles are normal when you start a new habit.
Thanks, Ana. I'll keep it up, and I'll stick to my plan.

title: Aula de direção
grammar: First conditional com unless e if not
reading: Tom is a learner, and today is his first driving lesson.
He holds the steering wheel with both hands.
“Don't touch the gearshift unless I tell you,” says the instructor.
At the crosswalk, Tom stops and waits for a pedestrian.
At the roundabout, he goes slowly and follows the speed limit.
He won't get his license unless he practices, but today he did fine.
dialogue: Tom, put on your seat belt. We won't start unless you're ready.
I'm ready, Ms. Cruz. Why is that light on the dashboard?
It's a warning light. It stays on unless the door is closed.
Oh, the door isn't closed! Sorry. Now I'm ready.
Good. Now turn slowly and stick to the speed limit. If you don't slow down, you'll miss the exit.
Can I use reverse here? I want to park near the curb.
Not yet. Look in the mirror first, and check for pedestrians.
Okay, I see one. I'll stop and wait here.

title: Experiência no laboratório de química
reading: Noah puts on his lab coat and goggles, and Mia takes the stopwatch.
She pours a clear chemical into a test tube.
“If you heat milk too fast, it boils over,” says Noah.
A little gas comes out of the flask.
If ice gets warm, it melts, and the table gets wet.
Noah spills a drop, but Mia says, “It's fine. Clean it up.”
dialogue: Noah, put on your goggles. This chemical can hurt your eyes.
Okay. What happens if I mix these two liquids?
If you mix them, they make gas, and the flask gets warm.
Sounds fun! Can I pour some into this test tube?
Sure. Go slowly, and use the stopwatch to count the minutes.
Interesting. I know that water freezes if the temperature drops to zero.
Right. Now put the cap on, and wash your hands.
Okay, Mia. Everything is fine, and I'm ready for the next test.

title: Esperando o ônibus escolar
grammar: When e as soon as com futuro
reading: Rosa waits at the bus stop with her little brother in his stroller.
It's cold and rainy, so she wears a raincoat and mittens.
The crossing guard stops the cars like a traffic cop.
Rosa's lunchbox is in her backpack.
The yellow shuttle bus is on time, and the driver always follows the speed limit.
When the driver comes, he will pick up the kids at the corner.
dialogue: Hi, Dan. Is the shuttle late today?
A little, but it's fine. The crossing guard says it will be here in five minutes.
I'm cold. When it comes, I'll sit near the heater.
Good idea. As soon as we get to school, I'm going to run to the cafeteria.
Me too. I forgot my lunchbox, so I'll buy lunch there.
No problem, I'll share my sandwich. Then I have to talk to the principal about the club.
Thanks! Look, the bus is here. When the door opens, we'll run!
Don't run! Walk slowly, and I'll hold the door for you.

title: Cardápio saudável na cantina
reading: Mia checks the school canteen menu today.
The fried dumplings have the most calories on the menu.
The baked fish has less salt and more protein.
The beans have the least calories and a lot of fiber.
At home, Mia cooks fried food in a wok, so she wants to cut down on it.
She buys beans, nuts, and a small pasta.
dialogue: Hi, Ben. What are you getting for lunch today?
I'm not sure. The fried dumplings look great, but I want to cut down on fried food.
Sure, the baked fish has less salt and more protein than the dumplings.
Okay. How about the pasta? Does it have a lot of fiber?
Not really. The beans have the most fiber, and they have the least calories, too.
Perfect. I'll take the beans and some nuts. Can I get them as takeout? My break is short.
Yes, you can. And take a drink with less sugar than a soda.
Good idea. I usually drink too much sugar.
Me too. I'm going to buy water and a small pasta for my sister.
Okay, let's go to the line, then.

title: Disputa de preços no mercado de rua
reading: Ana is at the street market with her brother Ben.
The butcher has good meat, but his price tag is a lot higher than at the store.
Organic melons are in season, but they cost far more here, and Ana says it's a rip-off.
Ben likes to haggle, so he asks the man to weigh a dozen coconuts again.
The man gives them a sample of the melon, and it's much sweeter than the last one.
Ana laughs because the deal is far better than before.
dialogue: Excuse me, sir. The price on this melon is a lot higher than yesterday.
Really? Melons are much more expensive this week, ma'am.
The butcher next door is much cheaper. Honestly, this looks like a rip-off.
Hold on! Let me weigh it again. Maybe the price tag is wrong.
Okay. Can you give me a better price for the melon and a dozen coconuts?
Hmm. I like to haggle, so tell me your price.
Eight dollars for the melon and the coconuts. Is that okay?
Deal! Eight dollars. Thanks for coming to my stall.

title: Quanto mais cedo, melhor
reading: Rosa is in a hurry because the meeting starts at nine.
It is rush hour, and a long traffic jam fills the street.
Drivers honk their horns, but nobody moves.
Rosa leaves the cab, crosses at the crosswalk, and runs to the station.
She swipes her card at the turnstile, and the monthly fee is already paid.
An announcement says the train is late, so the more she waits, the angrier she feels.
dialogue: Tom! Why are you running? The meeting starts at nine thirty.
I know, but the traffic jam was terrible. I left my cab on Main Street.
Come on, hurry up. The turnstile is on the left.
Done. Is the train late again?
Yes. The earlier you leave home, the easier the trip is.
You're right. The more I wait, the more nervous I feel.
Relax. We can read my itinerary and the guidebook while we wait.
Sure. Let's do it, and I'll buy the coffee.

title: Preparando o jantar para muitos
reading: Noah and Rosa are cooking dinner for twelve people.
They have organic peaches, but they don't have enough for everyone.
Rosa counts every ingredient on the counter.
Noah pours water into the pot and uses a whisk to mix the sauce.
The colander is big enough, but the skillet isn't big enough for all the vegetables.
Noah scoops the soup with a ladle, and the spatula turns the fish.
dialogue: Do we have enough rice for twelve people?
I think so. The big bag is full, but we need a measuring cup.
Here it is. Now, where is the skillet for the chicken?
It's small. We don't have enough space, so let's cook in two pans.
Okay. Hand me the spatula, please. I'll mix the vegetables.
Sure. Did you buy the peaches? They're in season now.
Yes, but only six. That's not enough for dessert.
No problem. Six peaches and some ice cream. I'll be back soon.

title: Quem é o vizinho barulhento
reading: Ben lives in an apartment with a small balcony and a long corridor.
He has a neighbor who stomps and thumps all night.
The noise level is high, and Ben's room is stuffy because the window is closed.
He talks to the landlady, a woman who lives on the first floor.
She asks the janitor, the man who fixes the lights, to talk to the neighbor.
Tomorrow the neighbor must keep it down, or Ben will leave a note on his doormat.
dialogue: Rosa, I can't sleep. The man who lives upstairs stomps at night.
That's terrible. Is he the neighbor who has a dog?
No, that's the woman who lives next door. This man just thumps around.
Did you tell the landlady or the janitor about it?
Yes. I even heard him snore through the wall last night!
Oh no. Come to my place tonight, and we can stock up on tea.
Thanks, but first I'll leave a note on his doormat: please keep it down.
Good idea. I'll call you tomorrow morning.

title: Achados e perdidos
reading: Rosa works at the lost property office at the mall.
Today the janitor comes to hand in a blue glove and a small mitten.
Rosa puts a tag on each thing and writes the date on a claim ticket.
She also finds a wallet, a handbag, and a gold earring.
She puts them in a shopping bag.
Everybody who loses something hopes to see it again.
dialogue: Good morning. Can I help you?
Yes, I lost a red scarf in a fitting room yesterday.
Let me check the shelf. Whose scarf is this one?
It's mine! I love it. My aunt made it. I also lost a thermos.
Great! Can you describe your thermos? We have three.
It's silver, with a tag on the lid. Whose gloves are those on your desk?
I don't know. A man handed them in this morning.
They look like my brother's. They have a small hole.
Then bring him here with this claim ticket.
Okay. I'll come back tomorrow with him.

title: Revisão: Jantar de domingo na casa dos pais
reading: Every Sunday, Tom eats dinner at his parents' house.
When the doorbell rings, the smell of roast is already in the hall.
His mother makes plenty of gravy, and she puts a warm loaf on the table.
The serving dish has a few potatoes and lots of beans.
Tom thinks this roast is better than last week's.
After dinner, there are lots of leftovers, and everybody takes some home.
dialogue: Tom, would you like some more roast and stuffing?
Yes, please. It's better than last week's.
Thanks. Did you take enough gravy?
Not really. Could I have a little more?
Of course. There's plenty in the pot.
Mom, did you bake from scratch again? This loaf is amazing.
I did. It's easier than you think.
Maybe I'll try it. Is there any pudding?
There's a little pudding, but we don't have enough napkins.
No problem. I'll get the jug and some napkins.

title: Fim de semana de lazer
reading: Noah and Lia spend the weekend at a campground by the lake.
Noah enjoys paddling his canoe, but Lia likes her red kayak more.
Before they cast off, they put on their lifejackets.
Noah doesn't mind carrying the firewood to the camp.
After they finish eating lunch, they go on a short hike.
At night they roast marshmallows, and Noah has a small sunburn on his nose.
dialogue: Lia, are you ready to cast off? The lake looks calm today.
Almost. I'm putting on my lifejacket. Do you mind carrying my paddle?
Not at all. Which boat do you want, the kayak or the canoe?
The kayak, please. I enjoy paddling alone, and you can take the canoe.
OK. We have to finish paddling before dark, though.
Don't worry. At camp we still have leftovers from last night.
Great. Did you bring enough firewood for the campfire?
Yes, I did. It's in the car, next to my safety vest.

title: Dormir bem
reading: Ben has insomnia, and he is always tired during the day.
He doesn't want to toss and turn on his old mattress tonight.
Drinking coffee after dinner is a bad idea.
Jogging in the park is good for him, and he can work out in the afternoon.
Now he changes the pillowcase, puts a warm duvet on the bed, and uses earplugs because his dog snores.
Going to bed at the same time every night helps a lot.
dialogue: You look drowsy, Ben. Did you sleep well last night?
Not really. Having insomnia is terrible.
Sorry to hear that. Maybe your mattress is too old.
Maybe. Sleeping on it feels like sleeping on the floor.
Drinking warm milk before bedtime always helps me.
Thanks. I'll try it tonight, and I'll hydrate more during the day.
Good idea. Does your dog still snore at night?
Yes, he does! That's why I need earplugs.

title: Rotina de manhã bem cedo
grammar: Verbos frasais sem objeto (get up, wake up)
reading: Noah's alarm clock rings before sunrise every morning.
He wakes up, but he hits the snooze button twice.
Then he gets up, wears his robe and opens the curtains.
Last Monday he overslept, so he got up late.
His friend Lia, a photographer, waited for him at the park.
Now Noah puts the alarm clock far from his bed.
dialogue: Noah, you're late again, sleepyhead! What happened this time?
I woke up at seven, but I hit snooze three times.
Three times? I always get up at six, even on Sunday. I'm like a rooster!
Really? My alarm clock is on the bedside table, so I can reach it.
Put it on the other side of the room. Then you have to get up to turn it off.
Good idea. Is the whole group already at the park for the shoot?
Yes, everybody is here, and we have your zoom lens.
Great! I'm sorry, Lia. Tomorrow I won't oversleep, I promise.

title: Descrevendo onde ficam as lojas da praça
grammar: Preposições de lugar: between, opposite, next to, behind
reading: The plaza in Jack's town is small but fun.
In the middle there is a fountain, and the gazebo is next to it.
The flagpole is behind the gazebo, and a street lamp stands next to it.
The bakery is across from the plaza, between the bank and the pharmacy.
The ice cream stand is opposite the bakery, near the crosswalk.
Jack reads the bulletin board, and then he eats ice cream by the fountain.
dialogue: Excuse me, is there a bakery near the plaza?
Yes! It's across from the plaza, between the bank and the pharmacy.
Thanks. And where can I buy a thesaurus? I also need a bookmark.
The bookstore is next to the pharmacy. You can't miss it.
Great. Is the gazebo in the middle of the plaza only for concerts?
Yes, on Sundays. The band plays behind the fountain, next to the flagpole.
Sounds fun! I'll look it up online. Is the ice cream stand near the crosswalk at the intersection?
Yes, it is. Come at six, and I'll buy you an ice cream.

title: Cuidado ao dirigir à noite
reading: Rosa drives home from the plaza at night.
There is thick fog, so she drives slowly.
The road is slippery, and there is a sharp curve ahead.
She turns on her headlights and sees a reflector in her lane.
Rosa brakes carefully and checks the dashboard.
Then she hears a short horn and smiles.
dialogue: Rosa, did you drive home from the plaza last night?
Yes, I did. The fog was really thick, so I drove slowly.
Really? Did your headlights work well?
Yes, but the wipers didn't work properly on the windshield.
That sounds dangerous. What did you do?
I stopped across from the newsstand and cleaned the windshield carefully.
Smart. You have to pay attention at night.
I know. Now I check my wipers before every long trip.

title: Gostos de série e filme
grammar: Advérbios de grau: quite, pretty, extremely, absolutely
reading: Ben and Lia watch a new series at night.
The plot is quite simple, but the characters are funny.
Episode one is pretty short.
Ben says the ending is extremely good.
Lia turns on the subtitles because the actor talks fast.
They decide to binge-watch the whole season.
dialogue: Did you see the new series everyone talks about?
Yes! I watched the first episode on Friday. It's pretty good.
Is the plot easy to follow? I'm tired after my lecture, and I have little time this semester.
Yes, it's quite simple. The characters are absolutely hilarious.
Really? Do you read the subtitles, or do you listen in English?
Both. The actors speak extremely fast, so I need the subtitles.
Good idea. My editor wants a review for the magazine anyway.
Great! Then let's binge-watch the first three episodes tonight.

title: Obras que ainda não acabaram
reading: The new plaza is still under construction.
Workers mix cement and push gravel in a wheelbarrow.
A big crane lifts bricks over a deep trench.
A bulldozer moves dirt near a tall scaffold.
The old gazebo no longer stands there, and a crack runs through the wall.
Noah still waits for the park to open.
dialogue: Mia, is the plaza still under construction?
Yes, it is. They need to build the new gazebo.
Really? I thought it was ready last month. I walk by every day.
I know. Now there's a bulldozer across from the bakery, and I can't cross there anymore.
That's annoying. Do you go to the cafe on that corner?
No, I don't go there anymore. The dust gets into my coffee.
Ha! At least you don't need a helmet.
True. But the scaffold is up until June, so be careful.

title: Mudanças recentes no bairro
grammar: Advérbios de tempo: recently, lately, nowadays
reading: Ana has lived in this neighborhood for ten years.
Recently, the city built a cycle path on the main street.
Workers painted a colorful mural on an old wall.
Lately, a big billboard stands next to the newsstand.
Nowadays the sidewalk is wider, but the cobblestone road still has a pothole.
New streetlamps stand at the crosswalk, and a green awning covers the storefront.
dialogue: Ben, have you seen the new mural on Pine Street?
Yes! I've walked past it every morning lately.
It's beautiful. Last year, there was only a gray wall.
True. And the city recently built a cycle path near the newsstand.
Nowadays I ride my bike to work instead of taking the bus.
Nice! Did they fix the pothole on the corner?
Not yet. The cobblestones are pretty, but they're bad for bikes.
I agree. Let's call the city about the pothole and the underpass tomorrow.

title: Perguntando ao concierge do hotel
reading: Lia arrives at a hotel in Chicago late in the evening.
A doorman opens the door, and a bellboy takes her suitcase.
In the lobby, there is a big mural of the city.
At the front desk, she gets her room key.
The concierge smiles and says, "Welcome! Your room has a balcony."
Lia is tired, so she goes to her room.
dialogue: Good evening. Do you know what time breakfast starts?
Yes, it starts at seven in the lobby restaurant.
Great. And do you know where I can buy a map of the city?
There's a small shop across the street. It's open until nine.
Thank you. Do you know how far the museum is from here?
It's about ten minutes on foot. Pay attention to the signs near the mural.
I will. Is there a luggage locker for my big bag?
Yes. The bellboy will keep it safe for you.

title: Dúvidas na fila do cinema
grammar: I wonder if / Can you tell me if
reading: Noah and Mia stand in line at the movie theater.
The line is long, and Mia is worried.
"I wonder if the thriller is sold out," she says.
An usher checks the tickets at the door.
Noah hates spoilers, so he doesn't read about the sequel.
The usher smiles and says the showtime is in ten minutes.
dialogue: Excuse me. Can you tell me if the eight o'clock showtime is sold out?
No, it isn't. But the front seat rows are almost full.
I wonder if there are two seats in the back row?
Let me check... Yes, seats five and six are free.
Perfect. Can you tell me if the movie has English subtitles?
Yes, it does. And the plot is easy to follow. The projector in room three is brand new, too.
Great. I usually binge-watch series at home, but I love the big screen.
Yes, you'll love it. The shop by the door sells popcorn. Enjoy the show!

title: Dúvidas sobre uma viagem em grupo
reading: Mia joins a group tour of the old ruins.
The concierge at her hotel booked it for her.
At the meeting point, she has to sign in with the tour guide.
The guide does a head count and smiles.
"You brought a raincoat, didn't you?" asks the guide.
"Yes, I did," says Mia, and she shows her canteen and binoculars.
dialogue: Ben, you're coming on the tour tomorrow, aren't you?
Yes, I am. Where is the meeting point?
It's at the hotel entrance. The concierge has the guest list.
Okay. The guide takes the group by bus, doesn't she?
Yes, she does. First we sign in, and then she does a head count.
Got it. You didn't forget your raincoat, did you?
No, I didn't. It's already in my backpack, next to my map.
Good. I have my room key, so I'm ready. See you at nine!

title: Revisão: Dia de esportes na escola
grammar: Revisão: -ing e to, passiva e comparativos
reading: Today is sports day at Lia's school.
Students sign in at the meeting point near the track.
The teacher does a head count before the first race.
Lia loves running, but she isn't as fast as Tom.
In the relay race, the runners pass a baton to each other.
The referee blows his whistle, and the sprint begins.
dialogue: Tom, where is our group? I can't find the meeting point.
It's behind the gym, next to the big tree. Everyone has to sign in there.
Okay. Do you know what time the relay race starts?
At two o'clock. I'm going to run the last part, so I'm nervous.
Don't worry. You're faster than me, and you love running, don't you?
I do, but the referee is strict about the jerseys, and the scoreboard shows everything.
Our team is going to win a medal, I'm sure.
Yes! Let's find the others and do a head count.

title: Amigos se ajudando
reading: Mia and Tom are best friends, but today they argue.
Tom forgot Mia's birthday, and she doesn't speak to him.
Tom knows it was his mistake, so he calls her.
He tells her the truth and makes a promise.
They apologize to each other and forgive each other.
Now they make up, and they trust each other again.
dialogue: Why didn't you call me on my birthday?
I'm sorry. I forgot, and it was my mistake.
We never argue, Tom. I'm really upset.
I don't blame you. I want to make up today.
Do you promise to remember next year?
I promise. We always help each other, right?
Yes, we do. Tell me the truth, and I'll forgive you.
Thank you! Let's have a small party at the venue tonight.
Good idea. I'll check the guest list and send the RSVP.
Perfect. And we can talk to each other all night.

title: Procurando alguém na multidão do festival
reading: Lia is at a music festival at a big venue with her friends.
Everyone wants to be in the front row by the crowd barrier.
The lineup is great, and the headliner starts at nine.
But Lia can't find her brother, and she doesn't see anyone she knows.
Someone waves at her from the lawn.
It's Noah, and he has a pair of earplugs for her!
dialogue: Noah, where are you? I don't see anyone I know.
I'm on the lawn, near the meeting point. Wave to me!
Okay, I see someone with a red wristband. Is that you?
Yes, it's me! I got this wristband at the sign in desk.
Nice. The headliner starts soon, and I forgot my earplugs.
No problem. I have extra earplugs in my bag. Do you want some?
Yes, please. And I already have a sunburn on my nose!
Ouch! Let's find shade near the campsite. Then everyone will be happy.
Sure. But first, I want to see the lineup.
Okay, deal. The first band starts at eight.

title: Procurando um lugar para estacionar
reading: Tom and Mia drive to a concert, but they can't find somewhere to park.
The parking lot is full, and there is nowhere on the curbside.
A sign says: you need a permit here, or they tow your car.
Cars honk everywhere, and the street is crazy.
Then they see a garage with a valet at the door.
The valet takes the car, and Tom is happy.
dialogue: Is there anywhere to park? I don't see a spot.
Not here. Everyone is looking for somewhere nearby.
Don't drive on the pavement! Just reverse a little.
Okay. Why are those cars honking at us?
Because we block the street. There's a garage near the wristband booth.
Good. Does it have a valet? I don't want them to tow the car.
Yes! He'll take the car, and we can see the lineup.
Perfect. I'll pay him now, and you can put on makeup inside.

title: Conectando ideias: apesar de
reading: Noah is stubborn, so he wants to hike in a rainstorm.
Lia is disappointed, but she goes with him.
Although the trail is slippery, they walk up slowly.
Their jackets are soaked, and their socks are damp.
Even though Lia starts to shiver, she keeps walking.
There is mud on their shoes, but they smile.
dialogue: It's raining hard, Noah. Are you sure about the hike?
Yes! Although it's raining, the forest is beautiful today.
You're so stubborn. We always argue about this!
I know, but even though it's wet, it's going to be fun.
Okay. I'm going to be soaked, so you must apologize.
Deal. I'll carry your duffel bag, and I apologize for the weather.
I almost fell in the mud. The trail is really slippery.
Let's keep going. The top is close, and the view is great.
Fine, although my feet are damp.
I promise! Let's carry on, and we'll rest at the top.

title: Resposta de um cliente insatisfeito
grammar: However e on the other hand
reading: Rosa answers a survey about the new store.
The jackets on the hangers are good quality; however, they are expensive.
The staff is nice. On the other hand, one cashier was rude.
She wants to complain, but she writes her feedback in a calm way.
She gives the store four stars.
In conclusion, she is a happy shopper, and she will come back.
dialogue: Did you fill out the survey about the store?
Yes. I wrote a long review. I liked the staff; however, the parking lot was always full.
Really? I thought the quality was great.
The quality is great. On the other hand, the prices are high.
True. Did you complain to the manager?
No, I wrote my feedback online instead. It's easier.
Last week one worker was rude to me. However, he apologized later.
Good. I hope they read it. In conclusion, we'll shop there again.

title: Atraso de voo e reclamação
grammar: Because of vs because; revisão geral de conectivos
reading: Tom and Mia wait in the terminal because of a delay.
The airline makes an announcement about the rainstorm.
The runway is wet, so the crew can't start takeoff.
Although they are tired, they stay at the gate.
They talk and play games, and they lose track of time.
Because of the delay, they will have a short layover.
dialogue: Why are all these people at the gate?
Our flight has a delay because of the storm.
How long? I hate waiting. The airline didn't send a message.
There was an announcement. We leave in two hours because the runway is wet.
Two hours! Although we're tired, we can't sleep here.
Let's get a snack and talk. We always lose track of time together.
Good idea. I like to pack light. My duffel bag is easy to carry.
Do you know if the crew is here?
Yes, they arrived early. We'll still make our layover in Denver.
Great. Then let's get coffee, and I'll pay.

title: Revisão: Roteiro a pé pela cidade
grammar: Revisão: preposições, passiva e verbos frasais
reading: Today Mia shows Noah around the old city.
They start at a big monument in the main square.
It was built in 1900, and it is visited by many tourists.
Then they walk through an archway into a quiet courtyard.
At the street corner, they wait at the crosswalk and cross the bridge.
From the rooftop, they see the whole city and a park like a jungle.
dialogue: Where do we start our walk, Mia?
At the monument. It's in the main square, next to a big fountain.
Nice. What is that carving on the wall?
It's an old carving of a ship. It was made by a local artist.
And how do we get to the courtyard?
Go through the archway, then turn left at the street corner.
I see a lamppost and a balcony with flowers. Is that the place?
Yes! Then we'll go up to the rooftop for the view.
Perfect. Do we need a permit to park at the curbside?
Yes, but the parking lot is free. Let's leave the car there.

title: Gostos em comum no encontro de amigos
grammar: So do I e neither do I
reading: Lia and Tom are at a small concert tonight.
The drummer plays a fast beat, and the crowd sings the chorus.
Tom hums along because he loves this playlist.
Lia likes old vinyl records, and Tom does too.
The singer picks up the mic and plays an encore.
After the show, they talk about the songs and the long delay at the door.
dialogue: I love this chorus. I always hum the lyrics in the shower.
So do I! I put it on my playlist last week.
Really? I don't like loud music at home, though.
Neither do I. I prefer quiet songs on vinyl.
Same here. My dad has a lot of old records in the garage.
Cool! Did you fill out the survey at the door? They want feedback.
Not yet. I don't want to wait in line again after that delay.
Okay, deal. And I hope they play an encore next time!

title: Passeio em ônibus panorâmico
grammar: Why don't we e How about + -ing
reading: Mia and Ben take a sightseeing bus in the city.
Mia takes the aisle seat, and Ben sits by the window.
The bus goes under a big archway.
Soon the road is bumpy, and the countryside looks green.
The scenery is beautiful, and Mia takes a lot of photos.
The bus will pull into a small town at noon.
dialogue: How about getting a snack? There's a snack bar at the back.
Good idea. I'm hungry, but the road is so bumpy!
True. Why don't we wait until we pull into the next town?
Okay. Look, there's an old monument near the lamppost. Can you see it?
Yes! Wow, it's so tall. How about taking a photo from here?
Sure, I'll take it with my phone. Tomorrow we can go hiking in the hills.
Nice! Is it far from the city? I don't have much time.
No, it's only an hour away. I checked the map this morning.

title: Fofoca no escritório
reading: Lia works in a busy office, and today it is full of gossip.
Ben said that the company wants to hire an intern.
Rosa said that Tom is going to get a promotion.
Tom said that he wants a raise.
Mia said that she can't spill the beans.
After that, Lia goes to the snack bar for coffee.
dialogue: Did you hear the new gossip? Ben said that the manager wants to quit.
No way! That is a big scandal. Is it true?
I'm not sure. Mia said that she heard it at the snack bar.
Hmm. Tom said that he is going to get a promotion and a bonus.
Maybe the new intern knows more. We can ask her at lunch.
Good idea. I want a good entree anyway. But please don't spill the beans in front of everyone.
Of course not. I only want to know the truth.
Same here. Let's find out at lunch.

title: Recados na secretária eletrônica
grammar: Told e asked em discurso indireto
reading: Tom plays his voicemail after work.
First he hears a beep, and then a short greeting.
The caller is Ana, and she sounds happy.
She asked if he could go to the countryside this weekend.
Then his ringtone starts, and the phone is ringing again.
Ana told him to call back fast, so he does not hang up.
dialogue: Hi, Ana! Sorry, I missed your call. I heard your voicemail.
No problem. I told you to call me back, and I asked if you were free.
Yes, I'm free. Your message sounded urgent, so I called right away.
It's okay. Mia asked me to invite you to the countryside this weekend.
Sounds fun! Is there any gossip? My inbox has no news.
Yes. She told me that Ben got a promotion! But don't tell anyone.
Wow, that's great news. I won't say a word.
Perfect. I have to hang up now. See you on Saturday!

title: Desejos de quem queria ter mais tempo
reading: Rosa has a busy job, and she has little spare time.
Her hobby is baking, but she bakes only on Sundays.
She puts a sticky tab on her favorite recipes.
At night, she writes in her journal.
Rosa wishes she had more time, so she looks at the stars.
She makes a wish upon a star and smiles.
dialogue: You look tired, Rosa. Was it a long day?
Yes. I wish I had more time for baking.
I understand. I wish I weren't so busy, too. I have no time for knitting or sewing.
Wow, you do both? I wish I could sew a button!
It's easy. I can teach you. Call me, and leave a voicemail.
Thanks! If I won the lottery, I would quit my job and buy a mansion.
Ha! Don't think about pie in the sky. Just save one hour a week, and I'll cook fish for dinner.
Good idea. I'll put a sticky tab on my calendar for it.

title: Revisão: Visita a uma fazenda de ecoturismo
grammar: Revisão: perguntas indiretas, tags, passiva e relativos
reading: Lia and Noah visit an eco farm for the weekend.
The barn is big, and a little lamb sleeps next to the hay.
A scarecrow stands in the field near the haystack.
The farmer who owns the farm shows them an orchard.
The corn is picked by hand in the harvest season.
In the morning, Lia learns to milk the cow, and Noah pushes a wheelbarrow.
dialogue: Excuse me, could you tell me where the barn is?
Sure. It's behind the orchard, next to the haystack.
Thanks. Do you know what time we milk the cow tomorrow?
At six. The rooster wakes everyone up early.
Wow, early! The harvest season must be busy.
It is. The corn is picked by hand, and the work starts at dawn.
I love it. It's my new hobby, and I have spare time this weekend.
Great! Come back for the harvest festival, and bring your friends.
I will. Can you leave a voicemail about the date?
Of course. I'll leave one tonight, and we'll have it lined up.

title: Antes de dormir e depois de acordar
reading: Ben always brushes his teeth before going to bed.
He puts on his pajamas after taking a shower.
His mom sings a lullaby before turning off the light.
After turning on the nightlight in his room, he hugs his quilt.
In the morning, he puts on his bathrobe after waking up.
Then he takes his toothbrush again before eating breakfast.
dialogue: You look tired, Ben. What time did you turn in last night?
Around midnight. I watched videos in my room for too long.
Oh no. I always put on my pajamas before watching anything in bed.
Really? I usually fall asleep in my clothes. My dad snores every night, too.
That's bad for your sleep. After brushing my teeth, I read for ten minutes.
Sounds relaxing. In my spare time I only play loud games, haha.
Try some soft music tonight before closing your eyes.
Good idea. I'll turn off my ringtone and send calls to voicemail tonight.

title: Opinião sobre dependência de tecnologia
reading: Rosa looks at her phone as soon as she wakes up.
She scrolls through her feed and waits for new notifications.
Her screen time depends on her mood and on the weather.
Last night, she listened to music instead of scrolling.
Her brother laughs at her addiction, but he loves his games, too.
Tonight she will unplug her charger and talk to him about the habit.
dialogue: Rosa, you're always on your phone. How many hours of screen time do you have?
About six hours a day. I know, it's a bad habit, and it gives me stress.
Yesterday you didn't hear me when I called you from the kitchen.
Sorry! I depend on my phone for work, but I also check my inbox and spam all day.
Let's try something. Tonight, unplug the charger and turn off the wifi.
Hmm. I worry about missing a message from my boss.
You can wait for the morning. Nobody calls at midnight, and you'll sleep better in your pajamas.
Okay, you win. I'll try it tonight, I promise.

title: Medos e talentos de um aluno novo
reading: Mia is the new student, and she is a little shy.
She is afraid of speaking in front of the class, and she blushes easily.
But she is very good at singing.
Today she has an audition for the school choir.
Her stage fright is strong, her hands are sweaty, and she feels nervous.
Noah is proud of her, and her fear gets smaller.
dialogue: Hi Mia! Are you ready for the audition?
Not really. I'm nervous, and all this stress makes me yawn.
Why? You're so good at singing. I heard you whisper a song in the hallway yesterday.
Thanks, but I'm shy in front of people. I'm worried about forgetting the words, and I stammer.
Everyone forgets words sometimes. Last year I almost ran away from the stage!
Really? What did you do to cheer up?
I took a deep breath and a gulp of water. I'm proud of you already, you know.
Thanks, Noah. Okay, I'm going in now, and I'll sing my best!

title: Tarefas domésticas e passatempos
reading: Saturday is chore day at Rosa's house.
She does the laundry and puts the clothes in the laundry basket.
Her brother likes to make a mess in the kitchen when he makes lunch.
Rosa grabs a broom and a dustpan.
After that, she makes the bed and does her homework.
Then they sit on a chair and rest.
dialogue: Look at this kitchen! Juice is all over the floor.
Sorry! I was making lunch, and the cup fell. Can you help me?
I did the laundry with new detergent, and I'm making the bed next.
Okay. I'll scrub the floor, so pass me the sponge and a towel, please.
Here. Sweep first, and use the dustpan behind the chair. I'll fold the towels.
Thanks. Chores give me so much stress on weekends.
Let's tidy up the living room first. Noodle soup always helps me cheer up.
Perfect! I'll do the dishes after lunch, I promise.

title: Revisão final: Retrospectiva do ano
grammar: Revisão final: todas as estruturas do bloco A2
reading: It's the last night of the year, and Ana opens her dusty scrapbook.
Every keepsake has a memory: a pebble, a magnet, a photo.
She is proud of finishing her degree, and she is happy about starting an internship.
There has been a lot of change this year.
She was afraid of speaking in public, but now she is good at it.
She looks back and gets excited about next year.
dialogue: Ana, what's that big book on your lap?
It's my scrapbook, like a diary with pictures! I look back at my year every December.
Wow, you keep everything. Is that a ticket from the concert in April?
Yes! Before going on stage, I had terrible stage fright. But I managed to sing.
I remember. I was in the front row, and I almost cried.
And look, this is a keepsake from my first day at the internship.
That small badge holder was a big milestone. There has been so much change this year!
True. I got tired a lot, but I'm very happy now.
So, what are you going to do next year?
I'm going to learn to paint, and you're invited to my first show. I'll save you a seat!
